text.p: Oil firm OMV AG, Austria's biggest industrial group, reported a nine percent rise in nine-month earnings on Tuesday and said it was on track to better 1995's record result and raise its dividend.
Group earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) climbed to 2.21 billion schillings ($209 million) from 2.03 billion at the end of the third quarter.
Pre-tax profit in the same period jumped 17 percent to 2.24 billion schillings but a heavier tax burden weighed on net profit, which was flat at 1.63 billion.

"There will certainly be a double digit (percentage) increase in earnings before interest and tax and pre-tax profit this year," finance director Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer told a news conference. He added that an increase in last year's 20 schillings dividend payment looked certain.
The figures were at the top end of analysts' expectations. Market watchers singled out OMV's plastics division for particular praise.
"Most divisions were as expected with the notable exception of plastics. Plastics was the star turn," said Neil Morten, oil analyst at James Capel in London.
"The (high) oil price, plastics and restructuring measures all played a part," said Wendy Anderson of Lehman Brothers.
Plastics posted steady earnings before interest and tax of 517 million schillings, thanks to strict cost controls and despite a 25 percent drop in prices that squeezed margins.
Chief executive Richard Schenz said the firm was pursuing a plastics joint venture with Spain's Repsol and said he hoped to strike a deal before the end of the year.
"Plastics has been the problem child in OMV's portfolio but these figures should make a joint venture a more attractive proposition to potential partners," said an oil analyst.
Most other divisions also managed to improve on last year's figures -- even the troubled chemicals sector.
Chemicals turnover dropped significantly following the sale of its Chemie Linz unit but earnings rose 19 percent to 441 million schillings.
Exploration & production, mired in losses last year, ended the first nine months 60 million schillings in the black, thanks in part to world oil prices near post-Gulf War highs.
Marketing reported earnings of 165 million schillings, compared with a 60 million schillings loss last year.

Refining alone failed to match 1995's earnings. OMV said the sector suffered from low petrochemicals prices and wafer thin margins. A switch in OMV's inventory accounting to the internationally accepted last-in, first-out (LIFO) also resulted in a one-off charge of around 320 million schillings.
Chief executive Schenz and analysts agreed that a heavy tax burden could cloud the near-term net profit outlook, however.

"OMV is victim of the government's savings package," Schenz said, noting that the tax rate for the first nine months reached 27 percent and was likely to rise further. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254 ($ = 10.57 Austrian Schillings)
